cargo_config:
# Packed relative relocations (decision D19) shrink the relocation table and
# startup work on GNU Linux, whose linker and C library support them.
[target.x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu]
rustflags = ["-C", "link-arg=-Wl,-z,pack-relative-relocs"]

protocol.build: cargo build --locked --profile dist; dist is fat LTO with one codegen unit, and .cargo/config.toml packs relative relocations on GNU Linux
protocol.peak_memory: Native parent wait4 ru_maxrss in KiB, whole workload child lifetime including setup and cleanup; excludes Python's inherited high-water mark; recorded, not budgeted
protocol.private_memory: peak heap in KiB, rounded up: the most memory a run's allocations hold at once, apart from the binary's pages. Each observation's command runs a second time with benches/runtime/heap.c preloaded, which counts malloc usable sizes; the timed run is never counted. GNU builds only
protocol.cache: warm filesystem caches; inputs created before samples and pre-read by driver; no cache eviction
protocol.order: one child at a time; fixed workload order within each round; all warmup rounds precede measured rounds

background_load.note: A process outside this work used about one CPU throughout (ps lifetime average 108%), and an unrelated agent process was also running; the one-minute load average was 3.06 before and 3.78 after. The workstation has eight visible CPUs and the campaign runs one child at a time. p95 times carry this load; p50 times match an earlier same-source campaign at load 1.98.

rejected_instrument.instrument: a counting global allocator inside benches/runtime.rs that updated two relaxed atomics on every allocation, reporting peak_heap_bytes in the driver result
rejected_instrument.reason: It slowed the timed driver workloads it counted. An alternating A/B of the same dist driver with and without it, 8 pairs per workload under the same load, gave these medians. Heap counting moved to a separate counted run of each observation's command with benches/runtime/heap.c preloaded, so timed runs are never instrumented.
ab_output: loop: median counting 2208.4 ms, plain 1894.2 ms, ratio 1.166
calls: median counting 353.1 ms, plain 303.1 ms, ratio 1.165

boundaries: Budgets apply to GNU dist campaigns on the reference host (D3) only; musl campaigns record no peak heap and are correctness smoke checks.
Peak heap counts allocations through malloc (usable sizes); thread stacks and other mappings are not counted. Peak RSS is recorded, not budgeted.
Thirty samples describe this host under its recorded load; they are not confidence intervals, production tail latency, or cross-platform results.
Scaling, bounded long-run memory, and release performance acceptance remain for item 249 and milestone 10.
